legacy_root.title: Resolve settings precedence across enterprise/user/project/local scopes
legacy_root.question: For each settings key this program depends on (enabledPlugins, disabledMcpServers, hooks, permissions, model), which FILE at which scope actually wins - given the measured trap that disabledMcpServers at the root of ~/.claude.json was inert while the real map lived per-project, and enabledPlugins lives in ~/.claude/settings.json not ~/.claude.json?

winning_scope_table.winning_scope: project overlays user per plugin id; local overlays project; managed overlays local
winning_scope_table.merge_rule: object overlay, later scope wins per plugin-id
winning_scope_table.behaviour_delta: plugin-loaded set contained probe-plugin@lab when only user settings.json set it true; after project settings.json set the same id false, loaded=False (sha beb0857c4b8e…). Swapping the booleans reloaded the plugin, so the winner is the project scope, not the token 'false'.
winning_scope_table.inert_behaviour: writing enabledPlugins false at claude.json root left the plugin loaded=True; no unload

winning_scope_table.merge_rule: root disabledMcpServers is inert; per-project list is the live disable set for user-scoped MCP servers
winning_scope_table.behaviour_delta: MCP server probe-mcp was live with an empty per-project disabled list; after projects[path].disabledMcpServers listed it, live=False (subprocess mcp_live=False). The same id written at claude.json root left the server live.
winning_scope_table.inert_behaviour: root disable left live=True; mutant that honours the root key went live=False (both-states: production silent, mutant fires)

winning_scope_table.winning_scope: merge across settings.json scopes; not exclusive
winning_scope_table.merge_rule: PreToolUse handler lists concatenate; later scopes add commands rather than replacing
winning_scope_table.behaviour_delta: dispatch list was [res0012-user-hook]; after local settings.json added res0012-local-hook, dispatch became ['res0012-user-hook', 'res0012-local-hook'] so the local handler actually fired alongside the user handler.
winning_scope_table.inert_behaviour: claude.json PreToolUse res0012-inert-hook was absent from dispatch ['res0012-user-hook']

winning_scope_table.winning_file: settings.json chain; deny from any honoured scope still denies
winning_scope_table.merge_rule: lists concatenate; DENY matches beat ALLOW matches
winning_scope_table.behaviour_delta: permission gate returned ALLOW for Bash from user settings.json allow; after local settings.json added deny Bash, verdict=DENY. User deny plus local allow stayed DENY (local allow does not erase a merged deny).

winning_scope_table.winning_file: <project>/.claude/settings.local.json over project and user settings.json; managed-settings.json over local
winning_scope_table.merge_rule: scalar replace from the highest settings.json-family file that sets model
winning_scope_table.behaviour_delta: model picker returned res0012-user-model from user settings.json; after local settings.json set res0012-local-model, picker=res0012-local-model. Swapping the two strings made picker=res0012-user-model, so local scope won rather than the string res0012-local-model. Managed then replaced local with res0012-managed-model.

claims.claim: enabledPlugins is honoured from the settings.json chain and is inert in ~/.claude.json root.
disabledMcpServers at ~/.claude.json root is inert; the per-project map is the live disable set.
hooks concatenate across settings.json scopes and are inert in ~/.claude.json.
permissions lists merge across settings.json; deny from any honoured scope still denies; claude.json deny is inert.
model is a scalar won by the highest settings.json-family file; ~/.claude.json model is inert.
These deltas are this program's throwaway-home consumer, not a spawned Claude Code binary on this Linux worktree.
claims.strongest_caveat: A later client binary run could disagree on list-merge edge cases; the disabledMcpServers root-inert trap is independently recorded in public issues and is load-bearing in the mutant control.

legacy_root.strongest_caveat: Observations are of this program's isolated consumer, which encodes published settings.json precedence plus the estate trap that root disabledMcpServers is inert. Live ~/.claude was not read. The Claude Code binary was not spawned.
